principles: BAUS is the primary authority for stone safety (calcium oxalate) — Jindal and Luke's diet are cross-checked against it, not the other way round.
Don't restrict calcium — pair calcium-rich food (paneer, curd, milk) with oxalate-containing food in the same meal; it binds oxalate in the gut.
Fluid target 2.5-3L/day, spread evenly, extra glass with every meal.
Sustainable deficit: ~500-750 kcal/day below maintenance (~2300-2900 kcal/day at 100kg) — not the ~1,230 kcal/day 'Luke's diet' level, which is too aggressive.
Weekday lunch is realistically salad/soup only (office) — dinner and weekends have more flexibility for cooked dishes.
favouritesKeepInRotation: Apple, banana, berries, oranges and most fruit
fineInModeration: Saag paneer — pair the spinach with the paneer's calcium in the same dish, keep portion moderate
Dark chocolate (small square, occasional — not the daily norm)
avoidOrMinimise: Wheat bran, strong tea/coffee in excess
Lay's kettle chips and shop-bought parathas/chips as a regular night habit — fine as an occasional treat, not the default
M&S dark chocolate protein cereal / cocoa-based cereals as an everyday breakfast — occasional is fine

weekdayTemplate.breakfast: Aldi muesli with milk or curd, or a piece of fruit + curd, or a homemade paratha with curd.
weekdayTemplate.lunch: Big mixed salad (lettuce/cucumber/pepper base, not spinach-heavy) with paneer, tofu or kala chana + olive oil-lemon dressing, or a vegetable soup with a slice of sourdough — realistic for office.
weekdayTemplate.dinner: Rajma, kala chana, bhindi, dal makhani or kali dal with rice or roti, moderate portion, with curd on the side.
weekdayTemplate.snacks: Fruit, curd, a small handful of roasted chana most days; kettle chips or dark chocolate as an occasional treat, not daily.

weekendTemplate.breakfast: Dosa/idli + sambar (home-made), or paneer bhurji with sourdough.
weekendTemplate.lunch: Khichdi, or a quinoa bowl with vegetables and paneer/tofu.
weekendTemplate.dinner: Saag paneer (moderate spinach portion, paired with paneer) or rajma/kala chana, roti or rice, curd.
weekendTemplate.snacks: Fruit, curd, occasional treat (dark chocolate square, kettle chips) if wanted.

tips: BAUS guidance: aim for 2.5-3L fluid daily, spread evenly, with an extra glass alongside each meal — dilute urine reduces stone-forming crystals.

Calcium isn't the enemy: BAUS advises keeping normal dietary calcium (dairy, paneer) rather than cutting it — pairing calcium with oxalate-rich food actually binds oxalate in the gut before it reaches your kidneys.
High-oxalate foods to keep occasional, not daily: spinach, rhubarb, beetroot, almonds/cashews, bran, cocoa/dark chocolate, strong tea.
Jindal principle: warm water with a squeeze of lime before breakfast supports digestion.
For L5-S1 spondylolisthesis: avoid deep forward spinal flexion and heavy twisting loads — core stability work (bird-dog, dead bug, glute bridge) protects the joint better than sit-ups.
Sitting numbness check: if you've been at your desk over 45 minutes, stand and move for 2 minutes — prolonged static sitting triggers the sciatic numbness, not activity itself.
Anulom Vilom, Bhramari and Ujjayi breathing (Jindal routine) work well as a 10-minute wind-down — helps sleep and lowers stress-driven cortisol, which also supports blood sugar control.
Prediabetic HbA1c of 39: pairing carbs with protein/fibre (roti with dal, not roti alone) blunts the glucose spike more than cutting carbs entirely.
Fatty liver, ALT already improving (67 to 45): keep added sugar and saturated fat down, and keep the walking consistent — daily movement is one of the few proven ways to reduce liver fat.
Sustainable pace beats speed: 0.5-1kg/week is the range least likely to rebound — matches your own goal of not yo-yo'ing back up.
Vitamin C caution (BAUS): keep supplemental vitamin C modest — high-dose supplements convert to oxalate. Get vitamin C from whole fruit instead (oranges, berries), where the effect is different.
Eye yoga day: palming, focus shifts and blinking exercises help offset a screen-heavy day.
Wrist strength: light dumbbells + the level-4 thera clay squeeze build grip gradually — little and often beats one heavy session.
Jal neti (twice weekly): use lukewarm saline, never plain tap water, and finish with gentle nose-blowing to clear residual solution.
